reviews.name: Priya Nair
reviews.text: Ten years of build-up paid off. The final battle had my whole theatre cheering, and the farewells hit harder than I expected.

reviews.name: Lucas Moreau
reviews.text: Three hours long, but it never drags. The time-travel middle act is fan service in the best possible way.

reviews.name: Hana Sato
reviews.text: A satisfying ending if you've followed the series. Newcomers will be lost, but this film clearly isn't made for them.

reviews.name: Marcus Bell
reviews.text: Fun and colourful with a genuinely creepy villain, though the jokes undercut some of the emotional moments.

reviews.name: Ananya Iyer
reviews.text: Jane's return was the highlight for me. The screaming goats wore thin after the third time.

reviews.name: Tom Riley
reviews.text: Not as tight as the previous Thor film, but a breezy, good-looking watch on a lazy evening.

reviews.name: Sofia Martinez
reviews.text: Season one is gripping and uncomfortable in a way that stays with you. Clay carries every single episode.

reviews.name: Rahul Mehta
reviews.text: Started strong, but the later seasons stretched the story far thinner than it needed to be.

reviews.name: Emily Carter
reviews.text: Tough to watch at times. Worth it for the performances, but go in prepared for very heavy themes.

reviews.name: Jonas Weber
reviews.text: Every episode ends on a hook. The multilingual cast makes life aboard the ship feel chaotic and real.

reviews.name: Isabel Costa
reviews.text: Moody, beautiful, and confusing in a good way. A real shame we only got one season.

reviews.name: Arjun Rao
reviews.text: The ending raised more questions than it answered, but the atmosphere is unlike anything else.

reviews.name: Megan Brooks
reviews.text: Funny, warm, and surprisingly moving. Debbie steals every scene she's in.

reviews.name: Kavya Reddy
reviews.text: I knew nothing about wrestling and still loved it. The half-hour episodes make it very easy to binge.

reviews.name: Daniel Okafor
reviews.text: A brilliant ensemble cast, and the 80s costumes and soundtrack are a treat from start to finish.

reviews.name: Chloe Martin
reviews.text: A cosy kind of spooky. The key powers are creative, and Keyhouse itself feels like a character.

reviews.name: Vikram Singh
reviews.text: Season one is the strongest. The family drama gets in the way of the magic later on.

reviews.name: Lena Fischer
reviews.text: A good weekend binge with my younger siblings. Not too scary, but still properly tense.

title: Money Heist: Korea – Joint Economic Area

reviews.name: Min-jun Park
reviews.text: Moving the heist to a reunified Korea is a clever twist, and Berlin is excellent in this version.

reviews.name: Neha Kapoor
reviews.text: If you've seen the Spanish original, this follows it closely. Still fun, just with fewer surprises.

reviews.name: Carlos Ruiz
reviews.text: Tight and fast-paced. The cat-and-mouse scenes between the Professor and Woo-jin are the best part.

reviews.name: Oliver Hughes
reviews.text: Feels like the comic come to life. The episode with Death is one of the best hours of TV I've seen.

reviews.name: Aisha Khan
reviews.text: Gorgeous visuals, and the quiet, distant performance as Dream is exactly right.

reviews.name: Mateo Rossi
reviews.text: Slow in places, but the standalone episodes are fantastic and worth the wait.

reviews.name: Grace Kim
reviews.text: The Crows are the real stars. I'd happily watch a whole show of just Kaz, Inej and Jesper.

reviews.name: Rohan Das
reviews.text: Great world-building and costumes, and Kirigan makes a very convincing villain.

reviews.name: Freya Larsen
reviews.text: Season two rushes through a lot of story, but it's still an enjoyable fantasy adventure.

reviews.name: Jake Morrison
reviews.text: I grew up with these kids. The finale wrapped everything up, and I'm not ashamed to say I cried.

reviews.name: Meera Joshi
reviews.text: The 80s vibe, the soundtrack, the friendships. Season four in particular is incredible.

reviews.name: Sven Andersson
reviews.text: The seasons got longer and bigger, not always better, but it's still an absolute must-watch.

reviews.name: Isla Thompson
reviews.text: Dry, weird, and very funny. The dance scene at the Rave'N lives rent-free in my head.

reviews.name: Pooja Sharma
reviews.text: A fun mystery with great gothic style. Enid and Wednesday's friendship is the heart of the show.

reviews.name: Lucas Silva
reviews.text: Season two goes darker and more ambitious. Some episodes drag, but the finale makes up for it.

reviews.name: Hannah Lee
reviews.text: Joe's narration is creepily addictive. You end up rooting for him and hating yourself for it.

reviews.name: Siddharth Menon
reviews.text: Season one is a masterclass in tension. Later seasons get wilder but stay entertaining.

reviews.name: Clara Dubois
reviews.text: The London season was a fun change of pace, though I saw the big twist coming.
